submitted.rationale: Index 8 (In 0.77, Sb 0.23) had the highest measured EQE, 0.40%. It sits next to In11Sb3O24 (Sb 0.214). MACE puts this phase on the convex hull, and MEGNet predicts an HSE gap of 1.9 eV, which is below the 3.2 eV photon energy. The other two points I measured, on either side, gave much lower EQE, so the peak is probably near this phase.

rejected.reason: Close to InSbO4. Measured EQE was 0.105%, about four times lower than index 8.
In-rich mixture of In2O3 and In11Sb3O24. Measured EQE was 0.127%, lower than index 8.
Not measured because the budget ran out. EQE fell as Sb increased from index 8 to index 17, so this region looked less promising.

consultations.verdict: Support: In11Sb3O24 (Sb 0.214) is on the MACE hull (Ehull 0) with MEGNet HSE gap 1.9 eV < 3.2 eV photons, so a single-phase absorbing film near index 8 (Sb 0.227) is plausible.

Support: InSbO4 (Sb 0.5) is on the MACE hull, and its earlier MEGNet gap of 2.2 eV means it absorbs 3.2 eV light. Index 17 (Sb 0.508) should be close to single-phase InSbO4, which lets me compare it with the In-rich index 8 (EQE 0.40%).

Mild support: MEGNet puts bixbyite In2O3 at a 2.2 eV gap, so it also absorbs 3.2 eV light. The measured EQE is higher on the In-rich side (0.40% at Sb 0.23 vs 0.105% at Sb 0.51), so I am testing the more In-rich mixture of In2O3 and In11Sb3O24 at index 3.
